question: If sin A = 8/17 and cos B = 15/17,find sin A cos B+cosA sinB:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The expression **sin A cos B + cos A sin B** follows the compound angle identity **sin(A + B)**.

Given **sin A = 8/17** and **cos B = 15/17**, notice they belong to the **Pythagorean triplet (8, 15, 17)**.

This implies **cos A = 15/17** and **sin B = 8/17** as they share the same hypotenuse 17.

Substituting values: (8/17 × 15/17) + (15/17 × 8/17) = 120/289 + 120/289 = 240/289.

**∴ The correct answer is 240/289.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** sin A = 8/17 and cos B = 15/17

**Formula Used:** sin(A + B) = sin A cos B + cos A sin B | cos²θ = 1 − sin²θ

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/a77e3ac6804a1c525e559c9d03b1fa2fcd920ba9f6730e05ed2af298835384d4.png] 

⇒ First, find cos A: cos A = √(1 − sin² A) = √(1 − (8/17)²)

⇒ cos A = √(1 − 64/289) = √(225/289) = 15/17

⇒ Next, find sin B: sin B = √(1 − cos² B) = √(1 − (15/17)²)

⇒ sin B = √(1 − 225/289) = √(64/289) = 8/17

⇒ Required value = (8/17 × 15/17) + (15/17 × 8/17)

⇒ Value = 120/289 + 120/289 = 240/289

**∴ The correct answer is 240/289.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Trigonometric Identities for Sum/Difference

sin(A ± B) = sin A cos B ± cos A sin B and cos(A ± B) = cos A cos B ∓ sin A sin B.

Pythagorean Triplets

Sets of three positive integers a, b, and c such that a² + b² = c². Common examples include (3, 4, 5), (5, 12, 13), and (8, 15, 17).

Range of Sine and Cosine

For any real angle θ, −1 ≤ sin θ ≤ 1 and −1 ≤ cos θ ≤ 1.</p
